title: Read-only role check blames the role for any change to the shared tree

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Observed 2026-11-11 (slicer wave 2): `ork wave start slicer s455 s450 s456 s451 s453` failed with "ork: spec check failed: spec-check changed the tree, and it is a read-only role". The change was another session filing slicer s459 on main (log entry 19:18:46, from ork's S335 spec work), not the spec check. Wanted: compare only paths the role could have written, or name the changed paths and their log origin in the error, and refuse to start a spec check on a dirty tree rather than failing after it.

Re-anchored 2026-11-18:

- The fingerprint is `git -C ROOT status --porcelain -- .` (`internal/engine/speccheck.go:88-97`), scoped to the project by S292 (done 2026-11-09). S292's owner answer (Q1, project-only, 2026-11-04) keeps the project's own `.slicer/` in the fingerprint. The s459 filing was in the same project, so S292 does not cover this case.
- A change between `baseline` and `before` is an outside change and is retried once (`errSpecStatusChanged`, `internal/engine/speccheck.go:100,257-262`, retry at `:189`). A change between `before` and `after`, while the role runs, is the hard error "spec-check changed the tree, and it is a read-only role" (`internal/engine/speccheck.go:351-375`). It names no path. The same pattern is in the spec draft (`internal/engine/specdraft.go:178,279`) and the carve (`internal/engine/carve.go:73,117`).
- The fingerprint compares status lines, so a dirty tree that does not change passes (`TestSpecCheckOnADirtyButUnchangedTreeIsFine`). Refusing to start on a dirty tree would refuse every spec check while the owner has uncommitted tracking edits on main, which is the normal state between commits; this spec does not do that.
- adj 28 (`role.readonly-fingerprint`, decided yes) keeps the fingerprint. Whether a change made only under the project's `.slicer/` while the role runs is retried like an outside change is open: per the owner's answer to `specs.readonly-tracking-change`.
- Not slicer's: slicer has no read-only role check.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/engine/speccheck.go:99-172` (specStatusAt leaves out the project's .slicer/, adj 476; statusChangedPaths and treeChangedError name the paths)
- `internal/engine/speccheck.go:310-330` (the fingerprint reads use specStatusAt) and `internal/engine/speccheck.go:455` (the read-only error names the paths)
- `internal/engine/gitpaths.go:14-25` (projectPrefixWith takes the Deps git binary)
- `internal/engine/specdraft.go:178`, `internal/engine/specdraft.go:300` (name the paths in the draft's error too)
- `internal/engine/carve.go:131`
- `internal/engine/speccheck_test.go:71` (`specHarnessStatusReads` serves a sequence of status replies and the project prefix)
- `internal/engine/specdraft_test.go`
- `internal/engine/carve_test.go`
- `internal/daemon/speccheck_test.go:642` (the git read sequence gains the project prefix read)
- `docs/design.md:326-345` (spec check read-only fingerprint)

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `internal/engine/speccheck_test.go`, with `specHarnessStatusReads` serving the status before and after the role:

- `TestStatusChangedPaths`: the helper, given before ` M .slicer/log.jsonl\n` and after ` M .slicer/log.jsonl\n?? .slicer/slices/s459.json\n M src/a.py\n`, returns `.slicer/slices/s459.json` and `src/a.py`, sorted; a line present in both is not listed; a line that went away is listed. Red today: no helper.
- `TestTreeChangedErrorCapsTheListAtFivePaths`: seven changed paths give `: changed a, b, c, d, e and 2 more`. Red today: no helper.
- `TestSpecCheckTreeChangeNamesThePaths`: the role run adds `src/a.py` to the status. The error is still the read-only error and ends with `: changed src/a.py`. Red today: the message is fixed text.
- `TestSpecCheckIgnoresProjectSlicerChanges` (adj 476): the role run adds only `?? .slicer/slices/s459.json` and ` M .slicer/log.jsonl`; the spec check passes on the first attempt with no retry. Red today: a hard error.
- `TestSpecCheckIgnoresItsOwnProjectsSlicerDirInASubdirectory` (adj 476): with real git and the project in `b/`, a write to `b/.slicer/` passes. Red today: a hard error.
- `TestSpecCheckFingerprintKeepsOtherSlicerDirs`: a change to `sub/.slicer/x.json` (not the project root's `.slicer/`) still fails. Guard.
- `TestSpecCheckNonTrackingChangeStillFails`: a change to `src/a.py` and `.slicer/x.json` together fails at once and names `src/a.py` only. Red today for the naming.
- `TestSpecDraftTreeChangeNamesThePaths` in `internal/engine/specdraft_test.go` and `TestRunCarveRefusesARoleThatChangedTheTree` in `internal/engine/carve_test.go`: the same naming for the draft's and the carve's error. Red today.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests and see each red for the stated reason.
2. Add `statusChangedPaths(before, after string) []string`: the path part of every porcelain line that is in one fingerprint and not the other, sorted and unique.
3. Spec check, spec draft and carve: when `after != before`, append `: changed PATH, PATH` to the error (at most 5 paths, then `and N more`).
4. adj 476 (`specs.readonly-tracking-change` = ignore, narrows adj 28): the spec check's fingerprint leaves out the project's own `.slicer/` (the status lines whose path starts with `.slicer/` relative to the project root). Spec draft and carve keep today's fingerprint unless they share the helper; say which in the report.
5. Do not refuse a dirty tree at start; the fingerprint compares changes, not cleanliness.
6. Docs: the read-only fingerprint paragraph in `docs/design.md` (named paths; `.slicer/` left out of the spec check fingerprint, citing adj 476 and its narrowing of adj 28). Changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S341 --text "..."`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- A spec check, spec draft or carve that fails the read-only check names the paths that changed.
- A spec check whose only change during the role is under the project's .slicer/ passes (adj 476).
- A change to any other path still fails at once, as adj 28 requires outside the scope adj 476 narrows.
- A dirty but unchanged tree still passes.

Commands:
- `go test ./internal/engine -run 'StatusChangedPaths|SpecCheck|SpecDraft' -v`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` exits 0.
- `adj lint` exits 0.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, message "S341: read-only check names the changed paths".
